title: The OSI Model: The Complete Beginner's Guide

scenes.narration: Seven layers. One journey. Let's ship a package across the world and see what each layer does.

scenes.heading: The shipping company
scenes.narration: You're sending a package from New York to Tokyo. At the top, you write the letter, that's the application. Lower down, it's packed, numbered, and tracked so lost pieces get resent, that's transport. Then someone reads the address and picks the route, that's network. Next, the local truck and its driver, that's data link. And at the very bottom, the road itself, that's physical.

scenes.heading: Names to remember
scenes.narration: Each layer wraps the data in a new name. Layer four makes segments. Layer three makes packets. Layer two makes frames. And layer one is just bits. Routers live at layer three, and switches at layer two.

scenes.heading: Common mix-ups
scenes.narration: Three mix-ups. The internet runs on T C P I P, and O S I is just a reference model. Layer seven is the network service, not the app itself. And encryption belongs to the presentation layer, not the session layer.

items.wrong: OSI is what the internet uses
items.right: The internet uses TCP/IP; OSI is a model
It's the service the browser uses

scenes.cta: Try the Courseiva OSI model lab
scenes.narration: So, to recap. The O S I model has seven layers, from physical up to application. Data is wrapped as it goes down: segment, packet, frame, bits. Routers work at layer three, and switches at layer two. Ready to practise? Try the Courseiva OSI model lab.
